title: Parkinson Disease Overview
content: Parkinson disease is a progressive brain condition that can affect movement as well as mental health, sleep, pain and other aspects of health. Movement symptoms can include slow movement, tremor, rigidity, involuntary movement, difficulty walking and imbalance. Non-movement symptoms can include cognitive impairment, mental health problems, sleep disorders, pain and sensory disturbances. Symptoms generally worsen over time, but their presentation varies between people. There is currently no cure, but medicines, rehabilitation and other therapies can help reduce symptoms and improve functioning and quality of life. Parkinson disease is a clinical diagnosis and should be assessed by appropriately trained healthcare professionals.
